drhp.business: Dabur makes and markets Ayurveda- and nature-based consumer products spanning health and wellness, everyday personal care and value-added foods and beverages. The business is organised into three Strategic Business Units - Consumer Care (Health Care plus Home & Personal Care), Food & Beverages (fruit-based beverages, foods and the acquired Badshah Masala portfolio) and International Business (organic overseas operations plus the acquired Hobi Group and Namaste Laboratories LLC). risks.note: The outbreak of war in early 2026 disrupted oil supply chains, drove up energy prices and triggered inflationary pressures worldwide; uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz and financial tightening slowed growth, and management flags global uncertainties and energy price volatility as key watchpoints for FMCG demand and input costs.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and energy price volatility

risks.note: Unseasonal rains and erratic weather, particularly during peak summer months, tempered demand for seasonal categories; consumption in the healthcare portfolio and brands such as Dabur Glucose was explicitly impacted by unseasonal rains and a shorter summer.
risks.risk: Weather volatility and seasonality of key categories

risks.note: Urban demand, particularly in traditional trade, remained under pressure in the first half of the year and recovered only slowly, making a large part of the India FMCG business dependent on a gradual and uncertain urban recovery.
risks.risk: Soft urban demand in traditional trade

risks.note: The expansion of e-commerce and quick commerce is rapidly reshaping buying behaviour and channel salience, requiring continual re-engineering of route-to-market, assortment and trade economics to avoid losing share in a shifting retail landscape.
risks.risk: Channel disruption from e-commerce and quick commerce

risks.note: Dabur describes operating in a highly competitive market where consumer connect is the key differentiator; sustaining market share gains depends on continued brand investment, innovation and premiumisation.

Global inflation is expected to inch up significantly on the Middle East war situation; the Company relies on judicious price increases, premiumisation and cost management, which may lag if input inflation accelerates.

Dabur has manufacturing presence across nine countries and sells in more than 120, exposing the consolidated business to currency movement, geopolitical complexity in certain regions and trade or tariff policy shifts.
risks.risk: International business exposure across more than 120 countries

risks.note: Rural demand, which trended ahead of urban markets, was aided by favourable agricultural performance, an above-normal monsoon, government welfare initiatives and GST rationalisation - a reversal in any of these would directly affect Dabur's rural-weighted portfolio.
risks.risk: Dependence on rural demand and the agricultural cycle

sk.overview: The India Hygiene Product Market, as framed by the Credence Research Report commissioned and paid for by the issuer, spans baby diapers, adult diapers, sanitary pads, wipes, cotton swabs, and tampons and menstrual cups. Baby diapers dominated with a 48.86% share in 2024 and sanitary napkins accounted for 32.53%, with growth driven by rising health and hygiene awareness, urbanisation, increasing disposable incomes, greater female workforce participation, and government sanitation and menstrual-health programmes.
